extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians, and instrument developers conducting or evaluating inter-rater/intra-rater reliability and validation studies of clinical and behavioral measurement tools
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, conducting and reporting studies that evaluate inter-rater and intra-rater reliability and validity of clinical/behavioral measurement instruments (scales, observational tools, diagnostics), including appropriate statistics, study design elements, and feasibility testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable reliability threshold (≥0.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability coefficients with values ≥ 0.60 were categorised as acceptable; values below this were considered non-acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear predefined threshold (here ≥0.60) when classifying measures as acceptable vs non-acceptable and report how thresholds were applied to different coefficient types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and reporting of Cohen's kappa / weighted kappa
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohen's kappa (κ) and linear/ordinal weighted kappa were used to quantify inter-rater agreement for categorical/ordinal items (examples show κ values spanning wide ranges, e.g., 0.52–0.95; overall kappas reported per side or domain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the kappa type (Cohen's, Fleiss', weighted), the value, and interpretive context; provide per-item and overall kappas where relevant and consider weighted kappa for ordered categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent agreement (PA) as complementary statistic
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent agreement (PA) was reported alongside kappa values (e.g., PA varied from 78.1% to 96.9%) to show raw agreement levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always report PA together with kappa because high PA can occur with low kappa (prevalence effects); present both to aid interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for continuous measures
rubrics_metrics.description: ICC was used to assess reliability of continuous or scale scores (examples: ICC values reported for IRP4s, DCI, BS; ICCs used to compare experts vs non-experts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select an appropriate ICC model/type, report ICC with confidence intervals, and interpret in context (e.g., ICC≥0.75 often considered good-to-excellent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and likelihood ratios for diagnostic validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic instrument evaluation used sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and positive/negative likelihood ratios to report validity (e.g., nitrite test sensitivity 90%, combined test specificity 87%, +LR 5.63).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When validating screening/diagnostic tests, report these metrics along with the chosen gold standard and prevalence context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cronbach's alpha for internal consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Cronbach's alpha was used to assess internal consistency of instrument dimensions (examples: most SCIP dimensions α>0.7; one subscale α=0.375).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report Cronbach's alpha for subscales/dimensions, interpret values (commonly α≥0.7 acceptable), and flag unusually low values that may indicate poor internal consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevalence- and bias-adjusted kappa (PABAK)
rubrics_metrics.description: PABAK was used where prevalence/bias might distort kappa (example: PABAK values reported 0.35–0.90 for BCT coding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider PABAK or other adjustments when prevalence/bias issues affect kappa; report both raw kappa and adjusted measures as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fleiss' kappa for multi-rater categorical agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Fleiss' kappa was used to assess agreement across more than two raters (e.g., Fleiss' κ and Cohen's κ used in pediatric Chicago Classification study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Fleiss' kappa (or equivalent) for >2 raters and specify which coefficient was used for which comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinded assessment and use of video recordings
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies used blinded designs and video recordings (e.g., an experienced physician and an inexperienced student examined patients in a blinded design; videotaped events were rescored) to reduce bias and allow re-rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply blinding where possible and use recorded sessions to enable repeat scoring, blinded secondary review, and intrarater reliability testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a gold-standard comparator for validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity was assessed by comparison against an accepted gold standard (e.g., NIDRR criteria for UTI) or established instruments (e.g., comparing PEDro to Cochrane Back and Neck tool).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and use an appropriate gold standard or established comparator when testing criterion or convergent validity; report concordance statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report both inter-rater and intra-rater (test–retest) reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies routinely reported both inter-rater agreement (between different raters) and intrarater reliability (same rater over time), often across repeated scoring sessions (e.g., two time points, two weeks apart).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design studies to measure and report both forms of reliability and specify time intervals and conditions for test–retest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report confidence intervals and measures of uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Some reports included confidence intervals for kappa and ICC (e.g., weighted kappa with 95% CI), and reported significance levels for comparisons (p-values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide confidence intervals (and p-values where appropriate) for all reliability coefficients to convey precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of rater experience/expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Rater experience affected reliability for some measures (examples: experts had higher interrater reliability than non-experts for certain diagnoses; inter-rater agreement independent of experience in other studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report rater characteristics, stratify analyses by experience where relevant, and discuss potential influence on reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot testing and iterative instrument refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruments were pilot tested and revised iteratively (e.g., scoring system developed, pilot tested, adjusted through two rounds prior to final reliability testing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform pilot testing and refinement before formal reliability studies; document changes and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual adjustment of automated/software-generated measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Software-placed landmarks or automated outputs sometimes required manual adjustment, which influenced reliability (example: manual adjustment of HRM landmarks prior to CC diagnosis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using automated measurements, describe any manual interventions required and assess how they affect reliability and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility assessment: acceptability, demand, implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Feasibility was evaluated using domains such as 'acceptability', 'demand', and 'implementation' (example: church audit tool and compensatory movement scoring included feasibility questionnaires).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess feasibility alongside psychometrics using structured questionnaires and report results to inform real-world applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design elements: sample size, number of raters, repeated measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability studies specified numbers of subjects, raters, sessions, and intervals (examples: 30 recordings × 11 raters × two readings; 18 raters scored videos twice 2 weeks apart; 5 judges scored 90 swallows across two time points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly report sample size calculations or rationale, number and selection of raters, number of repeats, and time intervals used for intrarater testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling homogeneous samples and prevalence limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: When items were too homogeneous (present in too few sites/subjects) kappa could not be assessed and percent agreement was used instead (examples: 42 items sample too homogeneous to assess Kappa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note and report when limited variability prevents reliable kappa estimation; consider alternative statistics or acknowledge limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine multiple statistical metrics for comprehensive assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies combined kappa, ICC, percent agreement, sensitivity/specificity, and Cronbach's alpha to present a multifaceted view of reliability and validity (examples across multiple abstracts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a suite of complementary statistics tailored to outcome type (categorical vs continuous vs diagnostic) to provide a robust picture of measurement performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, calibration and re-calibration to improve and maintain reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Baseline training/calibration by a 'gold standard' and subsequent re-calibration improved examiner consistency over time (examples: baseline calibration followed by one-year re-calibration improved ICDAS reliability; training enhanced reliable application of NGASR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include formal training and calibration sessions prior to data collection and plan for periodic re-calibration to sustain reliability; report training procedures and their effects.
